_comment: cat-harness's own declaration — RENAMED from `folio-assistant.config.json` on 2026-09-20. It always described the PLATFORM, and the platform is `cat-harness` since the owner ruled that the `cat-` prefix reaches the harness layer and stops before `folio-assistant-*`. Under main's one-config-per-instance scheme the FILENAME binds a config to an instance, so leaving this one as `folio-assistant.config.json` silently attached the platform's declaration to the CHECKOUT, which is a different instance. `check:instance-config` could not catch it — it verifies that a config's name matches some declared instance, and `folio-assistant` is one. Two tests in `voice-gate.test.ts` caught it instead, by asserting which instance activates no voice and which has no config at all; both answers had silently swapped. The platform is not a folio — it holds no papers, no Lean and no chapters — but content/docs/ IS a real document-profile corpus: the user-facing docs site, structured prose with no formalisation. Declaring it is what makes QA criterion scoping work on this repo's own content; without it `readDeclaredFolioProfile()` returns undefined, the third state runs every criterion, and the paper adapter's LaTeX-shaped axes fire `critical` on prose that never reaches pdflatex. See AGENTS.md 'Content types' and `content/pipeline/profile-check.ts`.
_adapter_comment: Consequence worth knowing before you change this: `src/index.ts` reads `contentType` to pick the MCP adapter too, so a platform checkout now serves the DOCUMENT adapter — it drops the LaTeX render, paper audit/QA/build/transform and Lean tool groups that `PaperContentAdapter` adds on top. That is correct here and close to free: this repo has 0 .lean files, no lakefile, and no paper content for those tools to act on. It is NOT free in a folio, where declaring `document` silently removes `lean_build` — which is why `src/index.ts` still defaults to `paper` when nothing is declared.
_readme_comment: There is deliberately no `readme.pagesBaseUrl` here. This repo's Pages address derives identically from the git remote, and writing it down as a literal only creates something that can drift if the repo moves — `scripts/tests/getting-started.test.ts` asserts the provenance is "git remote" precisely so a redundant literal is caught. Same rule as everywhere else here: resolve it, do not compose it.
